name: identity and session
reason: Identity factors with no artefact that states a procedure and an oracle. The covered ones are almost all enumeration, credential testing or object level authorisation, because those are what the tools in D04, D05 and D06 actually do. The lifecycle and recovery factors, which is where most real account takeover happens, are almost entirely unaddressed.

L06-001.note: Token claim tampering is adjacent to canonicalisation of an identifier across layers. It does not test whether two spellings resolve to one principal.

L06-003.note: Account enumeration by response difference will surface aliasing by accident, but email normalisation is not the factor being tested.

L06-006.note: Given a captured hash, both tools state a procedure and an oracle for storage strength: crack it or do not. That is the cost parameter answered empirically.

L06-007.note: Credential testing against a live login is the direct test of stuffing resistance, with success and lockout as the oracle. Medusa exists specifically for the per address rate limit case.

L06-008.note: The entry states response and timing differences as the oracle for enumeration, which is the factor stated as a test.

L06-009.note: Timing separation between existing and absent accounts is one of the two oracles the entry names.

L06-010.note: The test list names MFA coverage per path. A list is a name, not a procedure with an oracle.

L06-015.note: The WebAuthn entry is a semantics reference. Relying party id binding is described and not tested.

L06-019.note: Length, alphabet and the points at which the identifier changes.

L06-020.note: Fixation is a named test in both lists. No artefact here performs it with a confirmation step.

L06-021.note: Rotation on privilege change is named in the list without a procedure.

L06-022.note: Capture and replay of the whole lifecycle including logout is exactly this test: replay the captured cookie after logout and see whether it still works.

L06-024.note: The passive capture reports which storage carries session state, which answers whether the state is client side and therefore forgeable.

L06-025.note: Attribute and domain scope are inventoried by the capture and varied directly by curl, with the Set-Cookie scope as the oracle.

L06-026.note: Cookie attribute surface reporting answers whether the prefix convention is used, which is the whole check.

L06-030.note: Storage key inventory answers whether a token is reachable from script, which is the factor as stated.

L06-036.note: Run here on 2026-10-27 as obs-006. An object endpoint authenticated the caller and never compared the caller to the record owner, so bob read alice's note and alice read bob's. Controls: no token refused, unknown id 404, and the owner still able to read their own object.

L06-037.note: Enumerating object ids and tenant prefixes at scale is the direct test of predictability, with another user's object as the oracle.

L06-038.note: An action allowed through a path that skips the layer holding the check.

L06-039.note: Replaying as a lower role catches a list that returns items the same principal cannot open directly, which is the factor stated as a test.

L06-040.note: The matrix is built per endpoint and role. Field level authorisation sits below that granularity.

L06-041.note: The specification names scope narrowing as a requirement and provides no test.

L06-044.note: Downgraded from L2: the session identifier entry tests entropy and rotation points, while this factor asks whether a machine credential is shared across environments and valid in both. Different question.

L06-045.note: Reset token binding is a named item in the test list with no procedure.

L06-055.note: The authorisation test list names anonymous access as a case to check. No artefact performs it.

L06-058.note: Login CSRF is named in the authentication list. Sessions per identity are required to confirm it and no entry states that procedure.

L06-013.note: The TOTP secret recoverable from a data path rather than only the enrolment flow.

L06-014.note: A push approval accepted for a transaction other than the one described.

L06-054.note: A sync write accepted from a source without write rights.

L06-061.note: A downstream action taken on a claim the receiver never verified.
